messages.subject: Issue with digitizing - new list member
parts:
Through a new subscription to the list, we received the message below.

Have a look at the help file of digitize2d to see if you are inputting everything correctly. Also, have a look at older threads in the mailing list, which might have discussed similar issues.

If you don´t manage, and for the list to help you, you would need to tell us a bit more about what you are trying to do and how (i.e. R code).

Make sure to write always to the list´s e-mail, I almost missed this question because of being attached to your subscription to the list.

Cheers,

Antigoni


When I try to incorporate the images, only one reads. Also, when it comes to start scanning I get the following: > img <- readJPEG("C:/Users/AnaCelia/Pictures/Tdimidiata/img/PI066 IZ M.jpg", native = TRUE) > digitize2d("PI066 IZ M.jpg", nlandmarks=11, scale=0.7, verbose = FALSE) Error in which(flist == tpsfile) : argument "tpsfile" is missing, with no default According to geomorph, TPS File refers to the name of a "TPS file" to be created. I have put a name to create the TPS file, but I still see the same thing, Please, someboyd could guide me, where to read more about the errors that I am commenting on: 1. Input jpg files and 2. the use of digitized2d

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Fwd: Re: Issue with digitizing - new list member
parts:
Ana,

have a look at chapter 2 of the practical companion of Geometric Morphometrics for biologists, by Mimi Zelditch and Don Swiderski. You can find it here:

https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328215969_A_Practical_Companion_to_Geometric_Morphometrics_for_Biologists_Running_analyses_in_freely-available_software_Second_Edition

There is a whole section on data acquisition in R, where StereoMorph is recommended, and I would advise you to use that approach instead of trying with digitize2d. A detailed script is provided, so you should be able to implement relatively easily.

Good luck!

Antigoni

PS: In the future please communicate through the list, not directly to my personal e-mail. This way you can get more varied answers by other users, as well as by the rest of the geomorph team, and help others that might have similar questions.
